Qlog summaries keep profile/scope and counts; kind qlog pages traces, streams, loss-declarations, incomplete-records, contributions, ranges or final-sizes. Except traces, select trace_index; stream-specific facets also require exact stream_id and direction. Facts retain all-recorded-events-before-selection scope, and interval overlap or endpoint loss declarations do not prove retransmission or network loss. The api-surface view groups retained HAR requests by method, origin and format-rule path template; templated segments are inferences. It reads no headers or bodies and reports no query values. The environment-manifest view projects the same HAR requests on the primary origin (most JSON-like records) into a replayable tool surface: view {kind: "environment-manifest", template_rules: ["after-uid-literal", "opaque-token", "sibling-variance"], include_query_parameter_names: true}. Each tool has a deterministic name, a path template and parameters from the four format rules plus the selected opt-in rules, observed query parameter names, a value-free body shape for POST/PUT/PATCH, status and content-type sets and record ordinals; records are pointers into the parent, excluded groups carry a reason and three fixed unknowns are always stated. Templates, parameters and names are inferences; the view copies no header, cookie or body values and refuses parents inspected with sensitive values. A capture_browser_scenario parent that selected response bodies or header values projects the same way, one record per network transaction in request order; it relies on capture-time redaction of declared secrets instead of that refusal, and a transaction whose URL was redacted is left unrepresented. For a retained record use source: {kind: "retained-evidence", evidence_id: "<parent_evidence_id>"}. Use normalized_result.parent_evidence_id from a summary receipt. Source kind is required. Portable source uses {kind: "inline", evidence: <complete Evidence>}. The WASM summary gives validation, counts, WAT digest/length, tool profile and execution/network states without reading WAT text. Rows include canonical identity, retained source-range count and observation support states. For exact file/native facts and processing gaps, use view {kind: "javascript-facts", where: {paths: ["package.json"]}, property_keys: ["name", "operation", "analysis_status"]}. To discover field names without values, opt into include_available_property_keys: true with property_keys: []. WASM views use kind wasm and facet sections/imports/exports/candidates/glue/wat/headers/details/tool_profile; text facets use UTF-16 code units and source forms remain exact. Mach-O views use kind macho and facet entrypoints/architectures/build_metadata/load_commands/dependencies/imports/exports/segments/provenance; source_exhaustive false means unreturned rows may exist. Exhausting candidate pages does not establish global interface completeness. Managed artifact summaries preserve complete identity/classification, metadata status, module/MVID, frameworks, coverage and limitations without unrelated inventories. Managed pages use kind managed and collection references/resources/attributes, retaining source coverage and build-local token scope; page exhaustion does not establish complete metadata. Managed member summaries keep identity, selection with unmatched names, coverage and per-collection counts; managed-members pages use collection types/exported_types/fields/methods/member_refs/call_edges/field_accesses/user_strings and carry the source selection and coverage. Both offset and limit are required; a retained-inventory receipt supplies an initial page size. Follow coverage.next_offset until exhausted. advertised.name: identify_flutter_build

advertised.description: Identify a Flutter app's build facts by pure parsing: the Dart VM snapshot hash from every lib/<abi>/libapp.so AOT section (vm and isolate, cross-checked), per-ABI library digests, the engine library's GNU build-id, and any labeled Dart version or toolchain strings libflutter.so carries. advertised.name: inspect_dart_aot
advertised.title: Inspect Dart Aot
advertised.description: Inspect one ABI's Dart AOT snapshot inside an APK: the four snapshot symbols located through the ELF dynamic symbol table with their offsets, sizes, and section headers (magic, kind, length), the snapshot hash, and a bounded string-pool projection from the isolate data section (package: source URIs, dart: SDK URIs, identifier-like tokens) exposing the app's dependency structure. String-pool entries are byte-pattern observations, not deserialized cluster semantics; typed class and function recovery needs an SDK-specific parser. Omitted or complete detail returns the full observation. Select detail: "summary" for target/ABI/library identity, all snapshot headers, coverage and original lower-bound counts without string lists. The complete source stays retained; read returned strings via inspect_analysis_view with parent_evidence_id and kind dart-aot, collection package_uris/dart_uris/class_like_tokens, offset and limit. Exhausting pages does not imply complete pool coverage. No engine, no execution.

The renderer admits at most 1,000,000 combined terminal cells, computed as columns × (rows + scrollback); every resize uses the selected scrollback and must fit the same budget. Supply a smaller terminal shape when that product is too large; dimensions are never clamped. A command name resolves through the inherited PATH; the working directory defaults to the caller's current directory; host environment variables are inherited with scenario overrides. Environment keys cannot contain '=' or NUL, and REA_PROCESS_RUN_ID is reserved for process ownership. Filesystem snapshots are opt-in through filesystem_observation_paths. A positive finalization_ms makes a timeout or idle deadline send SIGTERM to the captured root through its start identity, keep observing, and send SIGKILL once after the interval; exit.finalization records each attempt with its delivery result and the observed exit, and cancellation still ends the run at once. The target runs with the current user's permissions; this is not a security sandbox.

executable.description: Command name or executable path to run.

terminal.description: The visible terminal and scrollback together must use at most 1,000,000 xterm renderer cells: columns × (rows + scrollback). Resize events use the same scrollback and limit.

finalization_ms.description: Milliseconds a target may keep running after SIGTERM when timeout_ms or idle_timeout_ms fires, before SIGKILL; 0 sends SIGKILL immediately. Both signals reach the captured root only while its launch-time start identity still matches; cancellation ends the run at once.

limits.description: Resource budgets that bound execution and retained output for this operation.

pattern.description: Literal text to replace in captured output; not a regular expression.

__schema14.description: The capture must preserve its canonical scenario, comparison, and normalization SHA-256 commitments; ordered capture timestamps and contiguous sequence numbers; before and final filesystem snapshots with truncation propagated; and exit-code consistency with deadline termination. The event journal is required; empty journals are valid. A non-empty journal must reference every captured observation exactly once with unique in-range references. These cross-field invariants are checked by REA after capture.

raw_terminal.description: UTF-8 bytes of original PTY chunks; whole chunks are retained or omitted.

rendered_terminal.description: Cumulative UTF-8 bytes of serialized state plus visible lines, evaluated from retained PTY input; whole frames are retained or omitted. When normalization exceeds a bound before the frame size is known, observed_bytes contains the exact total for size-known frames and unknown_size_frames counts the other omissions.

normalized_terminal.description: UTF-8 bytes of normalized raw-chunk text retained under output_bytes; omitted frames can have unknown final size when normalization exceeded an intermediate bound.
